judgment: 今日判断：AI 生成的代码与答案已经是主流生产路径，工程侧的应对正从「更仔细地读」转向「可验证的检查 + 按风险分级放行」。Claude Code 团队用自动评审、多代理投票与风险分层把人工审批压到每 PR 最多一人，同时盯住回滚率而不是读了多少行；Uber 的 Genie 则把内部问答做成检索、引用、评估、转人工的闭环。另一条线是边界：Snowflake 托管 PostgreSQL 用五个「本来合法」的特性串到系统级 RCE，说明托管与沙箱都不是安全边界，值得留意的是代理身份与权限治理、以及评审轮次这类收敛指标。

recommendations.title: How the Claude Code team does code review
recommendations.reason: 给出了代理写代码之后评审流程的完整可抄作业版本：从持续评审、多代理投票到风险分级与「回滚率不升」的验收口径，全是一线数据。
key_points: 6 月到 9 月合并 PR 翻倍以上，回滚比例下降超过 40%；Anthropic 单体仓库日变更从 5 月约 2500 涨到 9 月 3 万以上。

风险分级由变更决定而不是作者：低风险自动检查全绿即免人工，中风险一人，高风险两人；代理的批准永远不算人工批准。
评审必须收敛：有 CLI PR 一夜跑了 50 多轮，git blame 显示 59% 的被反复标记代码在首轮就已存在，团队因此开始跟踪 rounds-to-pass。
recommendations.full_analysis:
一句话判断：这是目前公开材料里最完整的一份「代理生成代码如何评审」的工程方案，价值不在理念而在那些具体阈值和失败案例。

1. 规模前提。Claude Code 约 90% 的代码由 Claude 自己写；Anthropic 单体仓库每天落地的变更从 5 月的约 2500 涨到 9 月的 3 万以上。在这个量级上逐行人工评审已经不可能，团队把目标改写成一个可测量的约束：大多数 PR 最多一个人工审批（可以是作者本人），且回滚率和事故率不上升。人工时间同时统计审批数、评论数和等人时长，回滚与事故是护栏指标——如果它们涨了，人工时间只是被搬到了修故障那一端。

2. 评审提前到 PR 之前。给 Claude 一个能运行的东西（测试、构建、与设计稿对比的截图），要它拿输出说话而不是声称完成；再用一个全新上下文的子代理审 diff。作者在开 PR 前还会跑几个内部 skill：找 bug、简化 diff、端到端验证行为。同一类问题被反复标记时，修的是源头——skill、lint 规则或 CLAUDE.md。CLAUDE.md 只写项目是什么、约定、目标与非目标，保持很短；REVIEW.md 由代码 owner 写这块地方什么算失败（文档是「它在撒谎」、配置是「它路由错了」），限制 nit 数量、列出可跳过路径，并要求给文件名和行号作证据。

3. 发现要经过验证才给人看。多个代理同时找 bug，再由另一组代理对每条发现投票，票数不够就不发；只涉及风格、诊断、清理的发现被丢弃，这些过滤器在上线前用自家 PR 做过 A/B。留下的按严重度排序，并标注 Important、Nit 或 Pre-existing，避免把历史问题算在本次作者头上。每条发现必须被回应：修掉，或写理由关掉线程。安全评审独立一路，有未关闭发现就不能合并。

4. 分级与责任。风险等级由分类器读变更决定，第二个分类器判断这一条是否还需要额外的人；敏感路径和 CI 工作流永远要人。只有仓库信任名单上的作者走轻通道，其他人一律需要第二个人；代理的批准不能占人工名额；发起这次变更的人视为作者之一，出了问题由他负责。批准只对具体 commit 有效，代理推新提交或手工解决合并后必须重新批准。

5. 噪声与收敛。团队按作者对评论的反应给每条评论归类（改了、说它错了、说这是有意行为、认为不重要），并拿已知干净的 PR 跑评审器，统计它会诱导人做出有害修改的比例。优先级写死为：先抓真 bug，再减少评审轮次。噪声对代理作者更贵——人会一秒挥掉一个 nit，代理会去改，于是又多一个 commit 和一轮评审。最刺眼的失败案例是一个 CLI PR 一夜跑了五十多轮才被作者叫停；git blame 显示约 59% 被标记的代码在评审器第一轮就已存在，它并没有不断发现新 bug，只是每轮多翻出几个旧的。团队现在同时跟踪 recall 和 rounds-to-pass，并改了重审策略（原文此处列表在抓取中缺失）。

我的推荐：如果你所在团队已经让代理开 PR，这篇可以直接当流程模板。先做三件事：给代理一个可运行的验证手段、把评审按变更风险分级、把「回滚率不升」写成验收口径。别急着追零人工合并——作者自己也说，他们还没有在指标恶化时自动收紧审批的熔断器。

recommendations.title: Frozen Privilege: Remote Code Execution in Snowflake-Managed PostgreSQL
recommendations.reason: 五个都有文档、单独看都合法的 PostgreSQL 特性被串成从普通角色到系统级 RCE 的完整链条，且逐条绕过了厂商已发布的所有缓解措施，攻防两侧的细节都值得读。
key_points: 起点只是非超级用户角色 snowflake_admin 的 CREATEROLE：PG14 起它能自授 pg_read_all_data / pg_write_all_data 这类预定义系统角色。
改写 pg_cron 任务表的用户名即可让调度器以 postgres 身份经本地 socket 无密码执行 SQL，再种下 SECURITY DEFINER 后门拿到超级用户。
用 LANGUAGE internal 重新绑定被按名字封禁的 C 符号（pg_read_file、pg_ls_dir、lo_export），再用 lo_export 覆写 postgresql.auto.conf 的 archive_command，每个 WAL 段落盘时以 postgres（uid 26）执行 shell。
Snowflake 已于 2026-06 在服务端修复；作者指出 RDS 的 PL/Perl、PL/Rust 与 Azure Cosmos 同类问题说明托管 PostgreSQL 的提权链是系统性模式。
recommendations.full_analysis:
一句话判断：这不是一个数据库漏洞的故事，而是一堂关于「托管服务的安全边界到底在哪」的课，链条里没有任何一步是未文档化的利用。

1. 起点低得吓人。Snowflake 托管 PostgreSQL 实例里，snowflake_admin 是非超级用户，唯一显眼的属性是 CREATEROLE。PostgreSQL 14 之后，光有这个属性就足以自授预定义系统角色，包括 pg_read_all_data 和 pg_write_all_data——这组角色没有「创建者」，也不需要超级用户授予。于是第一步就是给自己开全库读写，连 pg_authid 里的口令校验值都能读。

2. 用调度器换身份。拿到写权限后，研究者直接改 pg_cron 的任务表：这是一个普通表，但调度器无条件信任它，而且任务通过本地 socket 以任意指定用户、无密码执行。把任务的用户名改成 postgres，等调度器触发，就以超级用户身份执行了 SQL，并创建一个 SECURITY DEFINER 函数当后门——函数以创建者的权限运行，之后任何低权限角色调用它都等于以超级用户执行。全程没有调用被禁止的 ALTER ROLE ... SUPERUSER。

3. 被封的名字不等于被封的能力。超级用户只是到了厂商防守的边界：COPY ... TO PROGRAM、ALTER SYSTEM、pg_read_file 与 pg_read_server_files 全被挡住。研究者的转折点是问「这些函数是怎么造出来的」——用 CREATE FUNCTION ... LANGUAGE internal 重新绑定二进制里仍然存在的 C 符号，被按 SQL 名字封掉的原语立刻以新名字复活，且没有任何库内权限检查。pg_read_file、pg_ls_dir、pg_stat_file、lo_export 都是这样拿回来的。

4. 从读文件到执行命令。先用重绑定的读函数确认 postgres 是 uid 26，读到租户的 mTLS 私钥与证书，以及明文存放的租户 AWS STS 凭证。然后用 lo_export 把 payload 直接写到 postgresql.auto.conf——PostgreSQL 重载时读取的配置文件——把 archive_command 改成自己的命令。这个 GUC 在每完成一个 WAL 段时由 /bin/sh -c 以 postgres 用户执行，是最干净的服务器端命令汇聚点，正常需要 ALTER SYSTEM 才能改，而那条路已被封。另一条等价路径是直接写并编译一个 C 扩展，用 LANGUAGE c 加载。

5. 为什么这比一个 CVE 更麻烦。攻击落成后是一个数据库对象，不随创建它的凭证失效而消失，改密码没用；它以 postgres 身份运行，而 postgres 拥有整个数据目录，于是可以绕过数据库直接改堆文件——约束、触发器、行级安全、库内审计全部失效，也没有 SQL 语句可以记录；还能删改 WAL 破坏时间点恢复与备库复制，损坏 pg_control，或就地加密数据文件；本机日志也能改（集中外送的日志不受影响）。从防守方看，大部分动作发生在托管客户看不见的那一层。

我的推荐：Snowflake 客户无需动作，厂商 5 月 31 日收到报告、6 月 9 日确认并在发布前完成服务端修复。但如果你自己跑 PostgreSQL，这篇列出的加固清单值得逐条对照：把 CREATEROLE 当准超级用户对待、限制 pg_cron 只能以会话用户运行、禁止非平台角色创建 LANGUAGE internal 或 c 函数、保护 postgresql.auto.conf、用 SELinux 约束引擎。最重要的心智模型是：隐藏函数名只是把门把手拆了，能力还在二进制里。

recommendations.title: How Uber Built a Genie to Answer Questions Correctly
recommendations.reason: 把内部知识问答系统从 ETL、向量索引、服务链路到评估与转人工讲成一整条工程流水线，还有上线一年后的真实使用数据，适合当 RAG 系统的架构参考。
key_points: 内部支持频道每月约 4.5 万个问题，Uber 选 RAG 而不是微调：能先用现有文档上线，文档更新也不需要重训模型。
Spark 做抽取与切块（LangChain 切分、OpenAI 嵌入），索引写入自研向量库 Sia 与对象存储 Terrablob，服务节点（leaves）下载基础索引并同步快照。
每个召回结果作为独立子上下文并带源 URL，模型被要求据此作答并给出引用；不够自信时明确说不知道并转给平台 on-call。
上线一年 154 个 Slack 频道、回答超过 7 万问题，整体有用率 48.9%，节省约 1.3 万工程小时。
recommendations.full_analysis:
一句话判断：这是一份少见地把「知识怎么进来、问题怎么答、答错怎么发现」三件事都讲清楚的内部 RAG 系统拆解，亮点在评估和逃生通道，而不是模型本身。

1. 问题定义得很窄。Genie 服务的不是生产事故，而是平台团队在 Slack 里日复一日的技术支持问答：配置怎么改、报错什么意思、某个不熟的功能怎么用。Uber 内部支持频道每月约 4.5 万个问题，信息其实都在 Engwiki 和内部 Stack Overflow 里，只是散到让人宁愿开口问人。

2. 选 RAG 的理由是交付节奏。微调需要大量高质量、多样的样本和持续的算力，文档一变就得重来；RAG 可以先拿现有文档上线，知识更新只改索引。代价是知识准备本身并不便宜——抽取、切块、生成嵌入、建索引都要做对。

3. 知识准备是离线流水线。Spark 从各来源接口抽取内容，放进 DataFrame，每行保留源 URL、正文和元数据——源 URL 从这一刻起就跟着数据走，后面才能做引用。切块用 LangChain，嵌入用 OpenAI 模型、以自定义 Python 函数在 Spark 里并行生成。索引由 bootstrap 任务灌入向量库 Sia，Spark 任务构建并合并索引，成品放 Terrablob；服务机（leaves）下载基础索引并同步快照，从而把「建知识」和「答单个问题」彻底分开。

4. 在线链路与防幻觉。Slack 里的提问进 Knowledge Service，先转成嵌入、在向量库里找相近片段，再把每个片段作为独立子上下文连同源 URL 一起塞进提示词，要求模型只用这些材料回答并给引用。还有一条容易被忽略的约束：知识源是预先筛选过的，只纳入适合经模型处理和 Slack 回复的文档。引用能降低无依据回答的概率，但不能保证每条陈述都对——检索到的段落要相关、原文档要准确、模型要忠实转述，所以评估是架构的一部分而不是附属品。

5. 逃生通道与反馈。回答下面有继续追问、标记已解决、联系人工三个按钮；信息不足时 Genie 明说并指向平台 on-call，人工接手后 Genie 保持沉默。反馈分四类：Resolved、Helpful、Not Helpful、Not Relevant，区分了「部分有用」与「完全解决」、「答错」与「本就不该由文档助手处理」。反馈经 Slack 插件进 Kafka、落 Hive、进看板。评估用 LLM as judge，对回答查幻觉与相关性，也对源文档打分并给改进建议——文档不好，检索再准也答不好。

结果与成本：2023 年 9 月上线，一年内 154 个频道、7 万多问题、有用率 48.9%、约 1.3 万工程小时。成本可见性靠一个 UUID 贯穿请求链路传到 Michelangelo Gateway，可进审计日志并按调用归账。

我的推荐：适合要自建内部知识助手的团队照着拆解。最值得抄的是三处：源 URL 从一开始就与文本绑定、回答必须带引用、以及「答不了就转人工且机器人闭嘴」。48.9% 的有用率也提醒我们，这类系统的价值不在于替代 on-call，而在于把重复问题挡在前面。

items.title: Decoherence (48 minute read)
items.summary: Decoherence is the accumulation of locally valid but mutually incompatible or redundant models within a system. It causes the cost of change to be dominated by translating among those models and preventing unintended side-effects. Decoherence grows relative to the rate of change of a system, and it increases faster the more decoherent a system is, resulting in runaway exponential growth. It rules out the specter of runaway recursive self-improvement, as decoherence both prevents AI from improving in a bubble and limits the rate at which it can improve outside of it. However, it also introduces a new kind of disaster called Decoherence Collapse.
items.score_reason: Decoherence：系统内局部自洽却互相冲突的模型如何推高变更成本。
items.highlight: 作者把“退相干”定义为局部合理却互不兼容的模型不断堆积，使改动成本被跨模型翻译和副作用排查吞没；它随变更频率指数增长，AI 正加速制造，最终导致系统只能靠智能体勉强维持、且越修越坏。
items.excerpt: Decoherence grows relative to the rate of change of a system, and it increases faster the more decoherent a system is, resulting in runaway exponential growth. It is not a new phenomenon, and humans have always countered it through carefully finding ways to do more with less, unifying disparate patterns and models into a cohesive whole.

items.title: Humans approve intent, machines prove conformance (8 minute read)
items.summary: Gittifacts routes agent-written changes to auto-merge, quick review, or full review based on test evidence and repository policy, after a human approves the plan. Missing signals can only increase scrutiny, and feature flags make merged changes reversible. Auto-merge still relies on the submitting agent's test environment for some evidence, while evidence generation took 13 to 17 minutes per change on the project's own repository.
items.score_reason: Gittifacts：人批准意图、机器证明一致性，按证据分级放行合并。
items.highlight: 作者用一周做出 gittifacts：以 Change 取代 PR，人只审批意图与验收标准，机器用 CI、红绿测试与证据把变更分流到自动合并或人工审查，并以独立特性开关保证可秒级回滚和归因。
items.excerpt: On October 1st Cloudflare published ["We want you to build the next Git platform"](https://blog.cloudflare.com/next-git-platform-on-cloudflare/). It asks a few questions: how do agents coordinate, what happens when their changes conflict, how does their work get reviewed, and how do we record why a change was made. The bar it sets is several agents working on one repository at the same time.

items.title: Exposing AdFection: How Discover-Tech Turned Targeted Ads Into a Pipeline for Zero-Click Mercenary Spyware (30 minute read)
items.summary: Citizen Lab links Israeli ad company Discover-Tech to zero-click delivery of Candiru spyware through targeted advertisements. Its Controlium platform lets customers select targets by mobile ad ID, cookie ID, or IP address, then run JavaScript when an ad is rendered. At least 45 Al Jazeera devices were infected in 2024 and 2025. Nearly four billion bidding records show ads across almost 200,000 sites and apps. Google, IAB Europe, Beeswax, Vungle, and Eskimi cut Discover-Tech's access after disclosure. A separate actor, DARK CARTOGRAPHER, used the infrastructure to link advertising IDs with phone numbers.
items.score_reason: Citizen Lab 揭露投放投放链路被用于零点击间谍软件投递。
items.highlight: Citizen Lab 首度证实：定向广告可投递零点击间谍软件，Discover-Tech 用 Controlium 平台把广告变成感染通道，至少45台半岛电视台设备被植入间谍软件。
items.excerpt: This is the first-ever public confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered via targeted ads. We call the technique AdFection, and show how it was used to infect devices at Al Jazeera with Candiru’s spyware. We also uncover Discover-Tech, and show how the company helps mercenary surveillance vendors track and hack devices around the world.

items.title: HybridAgent Thinks in Latent Space and Acts in Text (6 minute read)
items.summary: HybridAgent is a research approach for training AI agents to reason internally using numerical representations instead of writing out every intermediate thought, while still producing text to call tools such as Python or web search and deliver answers. In tests, a 14B Qwen3 model trained this way scored 52.4 on GAIA versus 43.7 for a matched text-only agent, with estimated decoding costs falling from $470 to $176 per million questions.
items.score_reason: HybridAgent 在潜空间推理、在文本空间调工具。
items.highlight: 斯坦福等提出 HybridAgent，用 HybridLink 适配器让模型在隐状态推理与文本工具调用间切换，14B 在 GAIA 上以 52.4 超过文本 RL 基线 43.7，解码成本降约三倍。
items.excerpt: An agent doesn’t need to write out every thought as text; it only needs text when it calls a tool or talks to a human. That’s the bet behind **HybridAgent**, from Stanford, UIUC, and Together AI. The model reasons by feeding its own hidden states back into itself, then drops into ordinary text whenever it needs Python, search, or a final answer.

items.title: Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins (18 minute read)
items.summary: ECDSA, the most widely used elliptic curve cryptography standard, uses a "seed" parameter, provided without explanation or justification, to define the coefficient b of the curve.

items.title: How to Formalize All of Mathematics (16 minute read)
items.summary: It would be a terrible waste of resources to spend millions of dollars to formalize mathematics results in libraries nobody uses. Doing so could also disincentivize good research and productive use of AI, disrupt the social norms and practices research depends on, and set the field back decades. Several projects are now working to ensure formal libraries fulfill the community's mathematical goals. Within the next few years, most of mathematics will be able to be formalized in such a way that mathematicians can explore, build on, and make use of formal libraries. This will significantly extend their ability to develop and discover new mathematics.

items.excerpt: Mathematicians’ reactions to last week’s big OpenAI release range from excitement to frustration, but one thing is clear: AI has become remarkably good at proving theorems, both formally and informally. The successes in the formal realm have led AI enthusiasts to declare that now is the time to formalize all of mathematics as a legacy for future generations.

items.title: Will it be a golden age or a dark age for mathematics (and science)? (23 minute read)
items.summary: Large language models have demonstrated remarkable abilities in generating mathematical proofs. This could lead to a golden age where a new generation of scientists is empowered, new STEM expertise is developed, and an open, collaborative, and intellectually independent scientific enterprise is preserved. However, it could also lead to independent human scientific activity progressively weakening, the production of new knowledge becoming increasingly concentrated in a small number of hands, and knowledge becoming alien to human understanding. The future will likely be a combination of these scenarios.

items.excerpt: Large language models (LLMs) and the research systems built around them (and commonly known as “artificial intelligence”) have demonstrated remarkable abilities in generating mathematical proofs. While the quality and limits of these tools remain incompletely understood, their potential for accelerating discovery and enabling extraordinary advances in mathematics and, more broadly, across science and technology seems clear.

items.title: Exploring AWS Lambda Web Functions for building web applications (9 minute read)
items.summary: AWS Lambda Web Functions run standard Node.js HTTP servers without adapters, with each execution environment handling concurrent requests and streaming responses. Deploy it with one command or [AWS CloudFormation](https://aws.amazon.com/cloudformation/) and get a public HTTPS endpoint with no adapter layer and no servers or load balancers to manage.

items.title: What Requirements Don't You Have? (7 minute read)
items.summary: Elegant systems often gain simplicity and scale by accepting limits on freshness, coordination, or flexibility. Coding agents tend to invent extra requirements, so explicitly stating which compromises are acceptable can prevent unnecessary locks, checks, and layers of abstraction.

items.excerpt: When designing software, the requirements you don't have are as important as the requirements you do. Identifying what you can compromise on — what can be slow, or stale, or inflexible — is usually the key to an elegant design.

items.title: Big Fish: Exploiting a 37-Year-Old Kernel Bug in OpenBSD (4 minute read)
items.summary: Calif reported two OpenBSD vulnerabilities that enabled local privilege escalation to root. A signed 16-bit shared-memory attachment counter, dating to the original BSD sources, could overflow after repeated forking and wrap to a negative value. That enabled a use-after-free race condition. A separate out-of-bounds write gave the exploit a write-what-where primitive. The exploit worked with KARL, SMAP, and SMEP enabled, using heap grooming, SysV shared-memory manipulation, IP multicast socket allocations, and PTE self-referential mapping changes to reach kernel execution.

items.excerpt: Calif frequently publishes our offensive research and work, but we otherwise don't draw much attention to the defensive work we do — assisting open source projects with remediation, patch generation, cryptographic improvements, and internal engineering projects we carry out for our clients.

items.title: Heartbreaker: Metamorphic ransomware comes for macOS (13 minute read)
items.summary: Heartbreaker, a previously undetected Rust ransomware for Apple Silicon Macs, encrypts files in ~/Downloads with AES-256-GCM, persists through a LaunchAgent, and then rebuilds itself by mutating its own embedded source code and recompiling with Cargo to change its hash each run. Patrick Wardle found the rebuild fragile and noisy because it may install Rust on the fly, depends on a now-deleted GitHub framework, and uses a single hard-coded key that lets victims decrypt every file for free. His open-source RansomWhere? tool still caught it by flagging an untrusted process that rapidly writes high-entropy files, which shows why behavior-based detection holds up against mutating binaries better than hash-based signatures.

items.title: Frozen Privilege: Remote Code Execution in Snowflake-Managed PostgreSQL (10 minute read)
items.summary: Varonis researchers found that Snowflake-managed PostgreSQL's non-superuser snowflake_admin role could be escalated to OS-level RCE by chaining five documented PostgreSQL features, defeating every published mitigation without disabling any. The chain used CREATEROLE to self-grant pg_write_all_data and hijacked a pg_cron job to run as postgres. It then rebound blocked functions through LANGUAGE internal, exposing tenant mTLS keys and AWS STS credentials and allowing an overwrite of archive_command. Snowflake has fixed the issue server-side, but teams running their own PostgreSQL should treat CREATEROLE as near-superuser, block LANGUAGE internal and C function creation, and audit pg_cron jobs and SECURITY DEFINER functions.
